For each file, find EVERY string that can reach a player's screen, and report it in the structured output. That includes:
- chat/console messages: game.print, player.print, force.print, surface.print
- flying text (player.create_local_flying_text etc.)
- GUI: caption=, tooltip=, text= on LuaGuiElement .add{} or assignments, including strings inside localised-string tables
- commands.add_command name + help text, and every response string those commands print
- custom alerts, message dialogs, set_goal_description, chart/map tag names, anything else display-bound
- data-stage: localised_name/localised_description, prototype names/descriptions, setting prototypes
- error() messages and log() calls (classify as category 'error'/'log', visibility 'log-only' or 'debug' as appropriate)
- strings handed to other mods or external systems (remote interface return values that get displayed, Discord bridge payloads) → category 'external'

Include even tiny strings ("OK", "Cancel", "+", "▶", "×"). For icon/symbol-only strings add hazard 'symbol-only'. Do NOT report: code comments, table keys, event/style/prototype identifier names used only as identifiers, file paths, pattern strings for string.find, storage keys.

- status: 'localised' if it is already a {"section.key", ...} locale reference, 'partial' if a locale reference is concatenated/mixed with hardcoded English, 'hardcoded' otherwise.
- dynamic: describe exactly how it is assembled if not static — every '..' concatenation, string.format, table.concat, tick-to-time formatting, number formatting, player/team name interpolation. This is critical: concatenated sentences are the main localisation hazard.
- visibility: 'player' (any player sees it), 'admin' (admin-only), 'debug' (behind a debug flag), 'external' (leaves the game: Discord, RCON, files), 'log-only'.
- hazards, any of: 'concat' (sentence built by concatenation), 'plural' (text hardcodes singular/plural like "1 slot"/"slots" or picks between them in Lua), 'sentence-fragments' (reusable fragment strings composed into sentences elsewhere), 'rich-text' (embeds [color=]/[item=]/[font=] tags), 'server-side-string' (built into a plain Lua string before display, so all players would get one language), 'discord-mirror' (also sent to Discord/external where a LocalisedString cannot go), 'symbol-only', 'sorted-by-text' (list sorted by the display string), 'newlines' (embedded \n layout).

files_scanned must list every file you read (repo-relative), even ones with zero strings. In notes, mention anything structurally interesting for the localisation plan (helper functions that build messages, message pipelines, patterns repeated across files).

Your final output is consumed by a script, not a human — return only the structured data.

1	-- Multi-Team Support - compat/claustorephobic.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Compatibility with ClaustOrephobic (zzz-claustorephobic) by Braxbro
6	-- (https://mods.factorio.com/mod/zzz-claustorephobic). ClaustOrephobic covers
7	-- the world in banded ore via pure data-stage noise expressions, with an
8	-- ore-free clearing (~90 tiles at default settings) around each surface's
9	-- starting point. Because it is data-stage only, its worldgen and its
10	-- can't-build-on-ore collision layer apply to every team surface natively --
11	-- no chunk mirroring or runtime shims are needed.
12	--
13	-- What it does NOT guarantee near spawn, and what this module fixes:
14	--
15	--   • Crude oil. Oil is ineligible for ClaustOrephobic's banding (its patch
16	--     isn't AoE-minable), so it keeps its vanilla autoplace -- which never
17	--     places in the starting area. Teams would have to hike for their first
18	--     oil. We place one guaranteed crude-oil node at 300% yield, a set
19	--     distance out from spawn (mts_claust_oil_distance_tiles runtime
20	--     setting, default 64 tiles ~= 2 chunks).
21	--
22	--   • Water. ClaustOrephobic worlds are commonly rolled with water scaled
23	--     low/none to maximize the ore field. We place the same origin deepwater
24	--     hole the dangOreus compat uses, so an offshore pump always has a spot.
25	--
26	-- Each is placed from its own chunk's on_chunk_generated, AFTER clone_mirror,
27	-- so it survives the nauvis clone. The synced setting, constant amounts, and
28	-- a non-colliding search over identical terrain give every team's variant an
29	-- identical spawn kit (MTS's same-map-per-team goal) -- unless the admin
30	-- changes the distance between two teams' surface generations.
31	
32	local compat_utils = require("compat.compat_utils")
33	local voidblock    = require("compat.voidblock")
34	
35	local claustorephobic = {}
36	
37	-- The crude-oil node is targeted `d` tiles out from spawn on the same
38	-- diagonal as the water hole, where d is the admin-adjustable
39	-- mts_claust_oil_distance_tiles runtime setting (default 64 ~= 2 chunks:
40	-- clear of the base start, inside ClaustOrephobic's default ~90-tile ore
41	-- clearing). Read at chunk-gen time, so team surfaces generated after a
42	-- change use the new distance. Up to d ~180 the node's chunk falls within
43	-- MTS's radius-3 spawn pre-generation and exists before the player lands;
44	-- beyond that it appears when the team first explores that far.
45	--
46	-- Placement must keep the node (3x3 box included) inside its own chunk: it
47	-- is placed when THAT chunk generates, after clone_mirror has processed it,
48	-- and any part poking into a neighbouring chunk could be wiped by that
49	-- chunk's later clone pass. Hence the derived search radius and clamp below.
50	local OIL_YIELD_FACTOR  = 3    -- 300% of the prototype's normal (=100%) amount
51	local OIL_SEARCH_RADIUS = 13   -- max non-colliding search radius
52	local OIL_CHUNK_MARGIN  = 2.5  -- keeps the node's 3x3 box off the chunk border
53	
54	--- Placement derived from the current setting: the tile target (equal x/y
55	--- putting the node ~d tiles from spawn), the chunk index containing it
56	--- (chunk (c,c)), and the search radius that keeps results inside that
57	--- chunk (may be < 1 when the target hugs a chunk border: skip searching).
58	local function oil_placement()
59	    local d = settings.global["mts_claust_oil_distance_tiles"].value
60	    local t = math.floor(d / math.sqrt(2)) + 0.5
61	    local chunk = math.floor(t / 32)
62	    local off = t - chunk * 32
63	    local radius = math.min(OIL_SEARCH_RADIUS, off - OIL_CHUNK_MARGIN, 32 - off - OIL_CHUNK_MARGIN)
64	    return {x = t, y = t}, chunk, radius
65	end
66	
67	-- ─── Detection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
68	
69	function claustorephobic.is_active()
70	    return script.active_mods["zzz-claustorephobic"] ~= nil
71	end
72	
73	-- ─── Origin oil node ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
74	
75	--- Place one crude-oil node near `target` at OIL_YIELD_FACTOR richness.
76	--- find_non_colliding_position keeps it off water and off any resource
77	--- entity (water and resources both collide with the resource layer). When
78	--- no clear spot exists in radius (or the radius collapsed at a chunk
79	--- border), force-place at the target clamped into the chunk's safe band --
80	--- keeping the guarantee, and keeping the node clone-safe.
81	local function place_spawn_oil(surface, target, chunk, radius)
82	    local proto = prototypes.entity["crude-oil"]
83	    if not proto then return end  -- overhaul without crude oil; nothing to place
84	
85	    local pos = radius >= 1
86	        and surface.find_non_colliding_position("crude-oil", target, radius, 1)
87	        or nil
88	    if not pos then
89	        local lo = chunk * 32 + OIL_CHUNK_MARGIN
90	        local hi = chunk * 32 + 32 - OIL_CHUNK_MARGIN
91	        pos = {
92	            x = math.min(math.max(target.x, lo), hi),
93	            y = math.min(math.max(target.y, lo), hi),
94	        }
95	    end
96	
97	    surface.create_entity{
98	        name     = "crude-oil",
99	        position = pos,
100	        amount   = OIL_YIELD_FACTOR * proto.normal_resource_amount,
101	    }
102	
103	    -- Clear trees/rocks over the node's 3x3 footprint so a pumpjack can be
104	    -- dropped straight on it.
105	    for _, entity in pairs(surface.find_entities_filtered{
106	        area = {{pos.x - 1.5, pos.y - 1.5}, {pos.x + 1.5, pos.y + 1.5}},
107	        type = {"tree", "simple-entity"},
108	    }) do
109	        entity.destroy()
110	    end
111	end
112	
113	-- ─── Chunk hook ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
114	
115	--- Run AFTER clone_mirror so the water hole and oil node survive the nauvis
116	--- clone. The water hole goes with chunk (0,0); the oil node with the chunk
117	--- containing its target (see oil_placement for pre-generation coverage).
118	--- VoidBlock islands are skipped: they're tiny with out-of-map beyond, and a
119	--- ClaustOrephobic+VoidBlock stack has no autoplaced ore to compensate for.
120	function claustorephobic.on_chunk_generated(event)
121	    if not claustorephobic.is_active() then return end
122	    if voidblock.is_active() then return end
123	    local surface = event.surface
124	    if not compat_utils.is_team_nauvis_variant(surface.name) then return end
125	
126	    local cx, cy = event.position.x, event.position.y
127	    if cx == 0 and cy == 0 then
128	        compat_utils.place_origin_water_hole(surface)
129	    end
130	    local target, chunk, radius = oil_placement()
131	    if cx == chunk and cy == chunk then
132	        place_spawn_oil(surface, target, chunk, radius)
133	    end
134	end
135	
136	return claustorephobic
137

1	-- Multi-Team Support - compat/clone_mirror.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Generic terrain compatibility for any third-party mod that decorates
6	-- the real "nauvis" surface via on_chunk_generated and filters by
7	-- hardcoded surface name. When a chunk is generated on a team-N-nauvis
8	-- (or mts-nauvis-N) surface, this module:
9	--
10	--   1. Ensures the same chunk has been generated on real nauvis. That
11	--      synchronously fires every third-party mod's on_chunk_generated
12	--      handler (dangOreus, VoidBlock, Alien Biomes' autoplace, etc.)
13	--      against the nauvis surface, where their filters DO accept it.
14	--   2. Mirrors the resulting tiles + entities + decoratives from
15	--      nauvis to the team surface via clone_area.
16	--
17	-- Net effect: whatever the mod stack puts on nauvis, every team
18	-- surface gets the same. Per-team variety is traded for "same map
19	-- across teams", which suits the head-to-head race format MTS targets.
20	--
21	-- This handler is mod-agnostic. Adding a new terrain decorator does
22	-- not require any per-mod compat code on the MTS side as long as the
23	-- mod's logic ends up writing to nauvis. Per-mod shims are only
24	-- needed for runtime gameplay rules that fire AFTER chunk generation
25	-- (e.g. dangOreus's on_built_entity, on_entity_died, on_nth_tick) and
26	-- those tend to be small and stable.
27	--
28	-- Cost model: marginal cost per team chunk approaches 1× as the team
29	-- count grows, because nauvis is generated once per chunk-area and
30	-- amortized across all teams. The first team to explore a chunk pays
31	-- ~2×; subsequent teams exploring the same chunk pay ~1×.
32	
33	local clone_mirror = {}
34	
35	local CHUNK_SIZE = 32
36	
37	-- Mods whose generated chunks carry script-managed entities that clone_area
38	-- cannot safely replicate. For these MTS must NOT clone team surfaces — each
39	-- variant generates natively from its pinned per-base seed instead (see
40	-- surface_utils.normalize_variant_seed), which keeps terrain identical across
41	-- teams while leaving the mod's own per-surface generation and state intact:
42	--   • space-is-fake — demolisher territories on Nauvis; clone_area drops
43	--     segmented units (demolishers), so cloning wipes them.
44	--   • gridlocked    — per-chunk "gl-unclaimed-chunk" markers whose render data
45	--     is keyed by entity unit_number; cloning leaves an unregistered copy and
46	--     crashes its on_chunk_charted handler.
47	-- Auto-detected (no user-facing setting). Outer planets are already native, so
48	-- in practice this only switches Nauvis to native. Mutually exclusive with
49	-- surface-name-filtering Nauvis terrain mods (VoidBlock, dangOreus), which need
50	-- cloning to reach the variants.
51	local NATIVE_GEN = false
52	for _, mod_name in pairs({ "space-is-fake", "gridlocked" }) do
53	    if script.active_mods[mod_name] then
54	        NATIVE_GEN = true
55	        break
56	    end
57	end
58	
59	--- Identify a team-owned planet variant and return the source planet
60	--- name to clone from, or nil if the surface is not a team variant.
61	---
62	--- Two naming schemes are recognized:
63	---   • "mts-<planet>-<N>"     — Space Age per-team variant
64	---   • "team-<N>-<planet>"    — base 2.0 cloned surface (no Space Age)
65	---
66	--- The captured planet name is returned verbatim and is used as the
67	--- key into `game.surfaces` to find the source. This works for any
68	--- planet — vanilla (nauvis, vulcanus, etc.) and modded (lignumis,
69	--- maraxsis, muluna, etc.). The patterns deliberately accept any
70	--- non-empty planet name, so a planet mod registered through any
71	--- path (data:extend, PlanetsLib:extend, etc.) cascades through the
72	--- variant naming and lands here automatically.
73	local function source_planet_for(team_surface_name)
74	    if not team_surface_name then return nil end
75	    -- Space Age variant: mts-<planet>-<N>
76	    local planet = team_surface_name:match("^mts%-(.+)%-%d+$")
77	    if planet then return planet end
78	    -- Non-Space-Age clone: team-<N>-<planet>
79	    planet = team_surface_name:match("^team%-%d+%-(.+)$")
80	    if planet then return planet end
81	    return nil
82	end
83	
84	--- Hook from MTS's on_chunk_generated event. Cheap when the surface
85	--- isn't a team variant (early return). For team variants, drives the
86	--- matching planet's chunk to generate and clones the result.
87	---
88	--- Generalisation note: this used to be hardcoded to nauvis only. The
89	--- generalization to all planets means a chunk-decorating mod that
90	--- targets, say, Vulcanus (filtering by `surface.name == "vulcanus"`)
91	--- will see its decoration mirrored to every team's Vulcanus variant
92	--- with no per-mod compat code. dangOreus, VoidBlock, Alien Biomes,
93	--- and (vanilla) modded resource autoplaces all benefit equally.
94	function clone_mirror.on_chunk_generated(event)
95	    if NATIVE_GEN then return end
96	    local team_surface = event.surface
97	    if not (team_surface and team_surface.valid) then return end
98	
99	    local source_planet_name = source_planet_for(team_surface.name)
100	    if not source_planet_name then return end
101	
102	    local source = game.surfaces[source_planet_name]
103	    if not (source and source.valid) then
104	        -- Source planet hasn't been instantiated yet (Factorio creates
105	        -- planet surfaces lazily in Space Age). Without the source we
106	        -- can't clone; skip silently. The next chunk-gen attempt will
107	        -- retry, and by then the source surface should exist.
108	        return
109	    end
110	
111	    local cx, cy = event.position.x, event.position.y
112	    -- Drive the source planet to generate the same chunk if it hasn't
113	    -- already. Every mod that listens to on_chunk_generated for the
114	    -- source planet runs synchronously inside force_generate_chunk_requests.
115	    if not source.is_chunk_generated({cx, cy}) then
116	        source.request_to_generate_chunks(
117	            {cx * CHUNK_SIZE + CHUNK_SIZE / 2, cy * CHUNK_SIZE + CHUNK_SIZE / 2}, 0)
118	        source.force_generate_chunk_requests()
119	    end
120	
121	    -- Mirror tiles + entities + decoratives. clone_area is synchronous
122	    -- and overwrites destination contents, so any vanilla worldgen
123	    -- that happened on the team surface a moment ago is replaced by
124	    -- the source planet's (post-mod-decoration) state.
125	    source.clone_area{
126	        source_area         = event.area,
127	        destination_area    = event.area,
128	        destination_surface = team_surface,
129	        clone_tiles         = true,
130	        clone_entities      = true,
131	        clone_decoratives   = true,
132	        expand_map          = false,
133	    }
134	end
135	
136	return clone_mirror
137

5	-- Shared utilities for compat modules (vanilla, voidblock).
6	-- Extracts common logic: surface naming, teleport queue, display names,

8	
9	local helpers         = require("scripts.helpers")
10	local space_age       = require("scripts.space_age")
11	local planet_map      = require("scripts.planet_map")
12	local ultracube_compat = require("compat.ultracube")
13	local platformer      = require("compat.platformer")
14	local space_is_fake   = require("compat.space_is_fake")
15	
16	local compat_utils = {}
17	
18	--- True when an active compat keeps players permanently in remote
19	--- controller (no walkable character to Esc back to). Platformer is the
20	--- canonical case; future compats with the same constraint should OR in here.
21	function compat_utils.is_compat_remote_only_mode()
22	    return platformer.is_active()
23	end
24	
25	--- Default character starting items for vanilla / VoidBlock modes.
26	--- Mirrors the Factorio freeplay starting loadout.
27	compat_utils.CHARACTER_STARTING_ITEMS = {
28	    {name = "iron-plate",          count = 8},
29	    {name = "wood",                count = 1},
30	    {name = "pistol",              count = 1},
31	    {name = "firearm-magazine",    count = 10},
32	    {name = "burner-mining-drill", count = 1},
33	    {name = "stone-furnace",       count = 1},
34	}
35	
36	--- Capitalize first letter of planet name for display.
37	--- planet "nauvis" -> "Nauvis"
38	function compat_utils.planet_display_name(planet)
39	    return planet:sub(1, 1):upper() .. planet:sub(2)
40	end
41	
42	--- True for a team's nauvis variant under either naming scheme:
43	--- "team-N-nauvis" (base 2.0 clone) or "mts-nauvis-N" (Space Age variant).
44	--- Shared by chunk-gen compat shims (dangOreus, ClaustOrephobic) that
45	--- decorate each team's spawn chunk.
46	function compat_utils.is_team_nauvis_variant(surface_name)
47	    if not surface_name then return false end
48	    if surface_name:find("^team%-%d+%-nauvis$") then return true end
49	    if surface_name:find("^mts%-nauvis%-%d+$")  then return true end
50	    return false
51	end
52	
53	-- Deepwater hole placed near origin so offshore pumps always have a spot:
54	-- dangOreus shrinks the starter lake below the vanilla size, and
55	-- ClaustOrephobic-style ore worlds are often run with water scaled to none.
56	-- Offset diagonally from spawn (0,0) so players don't drown on landing,
57	-- kept entirely within chunk (0,0) so it's placed atomically.
58	local ORIGIN_WATER_TILE_NAME   = "deepwater"
59	local ORIGIN_WATER_HOLE_SIZE   = 4
60	local ORIGIN_WATER_HOLE_ORIGIN = {x = 3, y = 3}
61	
62	local ORIGIN_WATER_TILE_POSITIONS = {}
63	for dy = 0, ORIGIN_WATER_HOLE_SIZE - 1 do
64	    for dx = 0, ORIGIN_WATER_HOLE_SIZE - 1 do
65	        ORIGIN_WATER_TILE_POSITIONS[#ORIGIN_WATER_TILE_POSITIONS + 1] = {
66	            ORIGIN_WATER_HOLE_ORIGIN.x + dx,
67	            ORIGIN_WATER_HOLE_ORIGIN.y + dy,
68	        }
69	    end
70	end
71	
72	--- Place the origin deepwater hole on a surface. Call from chunk (0,0)'s
73	--- on_chunk_generated, AFTER clone_mirror, so the water overwrites cloned
74	--- tiles and removes any ore entities that landed on these tiles.
75	function compat_utils.place_origin_water_hole(surface)
76	    local tiles = {}
77	    for _, pos in ipairs(ORIGIN_WATER_TILE_POSITIONS) do
78	        tiles[#tiles + 1] = {name = ORIGIN_WATER_TILE_NAME, position = pos}
79	    end
80	    -- correct_tiles=true keeps water/land transitions clean;
81	    -- remove_colliding_entities clears any ore that landed on these tiles.
82	    surface.set_tiles(tiles, true, true, true, false)
83	end
84	
85	--- Process queued surface teleports. Must be called from on_tick.
86	function compat_utils.process_pending_teleports()
87	    if not storage.pending_vanilla_tp then return end
88	    if not next(storage.pending_vanilla_tp) then return end
89	    for player_index, surface in pairs(storage.pending_vanilla_tp) do
90	        local player = game.get_player(player_index)
91	        if player and player.valid and surface and surface.valid then
92	            helpers.diag("compat_utils.process_pending_teleports: TELEPORT → "
93	                .. surface.name, player)
94	            if player.teleport(player.force.get_spawn_position(surface), surface) then
95	                -- Player is now on their team surface. Run any post-teleport
96	                -- setup that depends on player.surface being correct.
97	                ultracube_compat.after_spawn(player)
98	                space_is_fake.after_spawn(player)
99	                storage.pending_vanilla_tp[player_index] = nil
100	            end
101	        else
102	            -- Destination surface is gone (retired/disbanded before this deferred
103	            -- teleport ran). Don't silently drop a live player onto nowhere -- put
104	            -- them on the landing pen if it exists, rather than leaving them on a
105	            -- team force with no home surface.
106	            if player and player.valid then
107	                local pen = game.surfaces["landing-pen"]
108	                if pen and pen.valid then
109	                    local pos = (player.character
110	                        and pen.find_non_colliding_position(player.character.name, {0, 0}, 16, 1))
111	                        or player.force.get_spawn_position(pen)
112	                    player.teleport(pos or {0, 0}, pen)
113	                end
114	            end
115	            storage.pending_vanilla_tp[player_index] = nil
116	        end
117	    end
118	end
119	
120	--- Create a personal surface for `player` and queue a deferred teleport.
121	---
122	--- Surface selection:
123	---   - With Space Age: use the team's Nauvis variant planet (e.g. "mts-nauvis-1").
124	---     This leverages the Space Age solar system so platforms travel between
125	---     per-team planet variants correctly.
126	---   - Without Space Age: fall back to a cloned vanilla surface
127	---     named "<force>-<planet>" (e.g. "team-1-nauvis") created via create_surface_fn.
128	---
129	--- `create_surface_fn(surf_name, planet)` is the fallback creator, called
130	--- only when Space Age is inactive and no existing clone surface was found.
131	---
132	--- Teleport is deferred to the next tick via storage.pending_vanilla_tp so
133	--- it is safe to call from on_player_created before the character is ready.
134	function compat_utils.setup_player_surface(player, create_surface_fn)
135	    local planet_base = "nauvis"
136	    local surface
137	    local surf_name
138	
139	    if space_age.is_active() then
140	        -- Use the team's Nauvis variant planet
141	        local variant = planet_map.get_home_planet(player.force.name)
142	        if variant then
143	            surface = planet_map.get_or_create_planet_surface(variant)
144	            surf_name = surface and surface.name or variant
145	        end
146	    end
147	
148	    if not surface then
149	        -- Fallback: clone the base Nauvis surface under a team-scoped name
150	        surf_name = player.force.name .. "-" .. planet_base
151	        surface = game.surfaces[surf_name]
152	        if not surface then
153	            surface = create_surface_fn(surf_name, planet_base)
154	        end
155	    end
156	
157	    storage.player_surfaces = storage.player_surfaces or {}
158	    storage.player_surfaces[player.index] = {name = surf_name, planet = planet_base}
159	
160	    storage.pending_vanilla_tp = storage.pending_vanilla_tp or {}
161	    storage.pending_vanilla_tp[player.index] = surface
162	end
163	
164	return compat_utils

2	-- Author: bits-orio

4	--
5	-- Compatibility with the dangOreus mod by Mylon
6	-- (https://mods.factorio.com/mod/dangOreus). dangOreus covers nauvis
7	-- with ore patches in varied patterns (pie, voronoi, perlin, random,
8	-- spiral).
9	--
10	-- Architecture
11	-- ────────────
12	-- Chunk-gen is handled generically by compat/clone_mirror.lua: dangOreus
13	-- runs on the real nauvis surface (where its hardcoded `surface.name ==
14	-- "nauvis"` filter accepts), and clone_mirror copies each chunk to
15	-- team-N-nauvis variants. We don't re-implement dangOreus's pattern
16	-- algorithms anymore.
17	--
18	-- This module retains only the runtime gameplay rules that dangOreus
19	-- applies AFTER chunk generation, scoped to team surfaces (since
20	-- dangOreus's own runtime handlers also filter by name and reject
21	-- team surfaces):
22	--
23	--   • on_built_entity     — block non-miner buildings on ore tiles
24	--   • on_entity_died      — spill resources from destroyed containers
25	--   • on_nth_tick         — floor-is-lava damage on ore-dense areas
26	--
27	-- Plus a small chunk-gen post-step that places a deepwater hole near
28	-- spawn so offshore pumps work even when dangOreus's starting-radius
29	-- is shrunk below the vanilla starter lake.
30	
31	local compat_utils = require("compat.compat_utils")
32	
33	local dangoreus = {}
34	
35	-- ─── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
36	
37	local DANGORE_EXCEPTIONS = {
38	    ["mining-drill"]     = true,
39	    ["car"]              = true,
40	    ["spider-vehicle"]   = true,
41	    ["locomotive"]       = true,
42	    ["cargo-wagon"]      = true,
43	    ["fluid-wagon"]      = true,
44	    ["artillery-wagon"]  = true,
45	    ["tile-ghost"]       = true,
46	    ["rail-support"]     = true,
47	    ["rail-ramp"]        = true,
48	    ["rail-signal"]      = true,
49	    ["rail-chain-signal"]= true,
50	}
51	
52	local DANGORE_EASY_EXCEPTIONS = {
53	    ["transport-belt"]     = true,
54	    ["underground-belt"]   = true,
55	    ["splitter"]           = true,
56	    ["electric-pole"]      = true,
57	    ["container"]          = true,
58	    ["logistic-container"] = true,
59	    ["pipe"]               = true,
60	    ["pipe-to-ground"]     = true,
61	    ["pump"]               = true,
62	    ["wall"]               = true,
63	    ["gate"]               = true,
64	    ["inserter"]           = true,
65	}
66	
67	-- ─── Detection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
68	
69	function dangoreus.is_active()
70	    return script.active_mods["dangOreus"] ~= nil
71	end
72	
73	--- Should this surface be treated as a team nauvis clone / variant?
74	--- Mirrors the patterns clone_mirror uses for chunk-gen.
75	dangoreus.is_enabled_surface = compat_utils.is_team_nauvis_variant
76	
77	-- ─── Storage ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
78	
79	function dangoreus.init_storage()
80	    storage.dangoreus = storage.dangoreus or {}
81	    -- flOre tracks per-player escalation distance for floor-is-lava.
82	    storage.dangoreus.flOre = storage.dangoreus.flOre or {}
83	end
84	
85	function dangoreus.init()
86	    dangoreus.init_storage()
87	    -- Earlier MTS versions called toggle("nauvis", false) to skip
88	    -- dangOreus's work on nauvis since no team played there. Under
89	    -- clone_mirror, nauvis IS the source of truth — its decorated
90	    -- chunks get copied to team surfaces. Re-enable to undo any
91	    -- legacy disable left over in saves upgrading from a pre-clone
92	    -- MTS version. Wrapped in pcall in case dangOreus's remote
93	    -- interface signature differs across versions.
94	    if dangoreus.is_active() then
95	        pcall(function()
96	            remote.call("dangOreus", "toggle", "nauvis", true)
97	        end)
98	    end
99	end
100	
101	-- ─── Origin water hole ────────────────────────────────────────────────
102	
103	--- Run AFTER clone_mirror so the water hole overwrites cloned tiles
104	--- and ore at the spawn pump location. Only runs for the chunk
105	--- containing origin.
106	function dangoreus.on_chunk_generated(event)
107	    if not dangoreus.is_active() then return end
108	    local surface = event.surface
109	    if not dangoreus.is_enabled_surface(surface.name) then return end
110	    if event.area.left_top.x ~= 0 or event.area.left_top.y ~= 0 then return end
111	    compat_utils.place_origin_water_hole(surface)
112	end
113	
114	-- ─── Anti-building on ore ─────────────────────────────────────────────
115	
116	function dangoreus.on_built_entity(event)
117	    local entity = event.created_entity or event.entity
118	    if not (entity and entity.valid) then return end
119	    if not dangoreus.is_enabled_surface(entity.surface.name) then return end
120	
121	    local entity_name, entity_type = entity.name, entity.type
122	    if entity_name == "entity-ghost" then
123	        entity_name, entity_type = entity.ghost_name, entity.ghost_type
124	    end
125	
126	    if DANGORE_EXCEPTIONS[entity_name] or DANGORE_EXCEPTIONS[entity_type] then return end
127	    if string.find(entity_type, "elevated") then return end
128	
129	    if settings.global["easy-mode"].value
130	       and (DANGORE_EASY_EXCEPTIONS[entity_name]
131	            or DANGORE_EASY_EXCEPTIONS[entity_type]
132	            or string.find(entity_type, "rail")
133	            or string.find(entity_type, "turret")) then
134	        return
135	    end
136	
137	    if entity.bounding_box.left_top.x == entity.bounding_box.right_bottom.x
138	       or entity.bounding_box.left_top.y == entity.bounding_box.right_bottom.y then
139	        return
140	    end
141	
142	    local last_user = entity.last_user
143	    local ores = entity.surface.count_entities_filtered{
144	        type = "resource", area = entity.bounding_box,
145	    }
146	    if ores > 0 then
147	        local force = entity.force
148	        local ttl = force.create_ghost_on_entity_death
149	        force.create_ghost_on_entity_death = false
150	        entity.die()
151	        force.create_ghost_on_entity_death = ttl
152	        if last_user then
153	            last_user.print("Cannot build non-miners on resources!")
154	        end
155	    end
156	end
157	
158	-- ─── Spill on destroyed container ─────────────────────────────────────
159	
160	function dangoreus.on_entity_died(event)
161	    local entity = event.entity
162	    if not (entity and entity.valid) then return end
163	    if not dangoreus.is_enabled_surface(entity.surface.name) then return end
164	    if script.active_mods["SpilledItems"] then return end
165	
166	    local t = entity.type
167	    if t == "container" or t == "cargo-wagon"
168	       or t == "logistic-container" or t == "car" then
169	        for i = 1, 255 do
170	            local inv = entity.get_inventory(i)
171	            if inv then
172	                for _, stack in pairs(inv.get_contents()) do
173	                    entity.surface.spill_item_stack{
174	                        position = entity.position, stack = stack,
175	                    }
176	                end
177	            end
178	        end
179	    end
180	end
181	
182	-- ─── Floor-is-lava ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
183	
184	function dangoreus.on_nth_tick()
185	    if not dangoreus.is_active() then return end
186	    if not settings.global["floor-is-lava"].value then return end
187	    storage.dangoreus = storage.dangoreus or {}
188	    storage.dangoreus.flOre = storage.dangoreus.flOre or {}
189	
190	    local easy_radius = settings.global["simple-ore-radius"].value
191	    for _, p in pairs(game.connected_players) do
192	        if p.character and dangoreus.is_enabled_surface(p.surface.name) then
193	            local position = p.character.position
194	            if math.abs(position.x) > easy_radius or math.abs(position.y) > easy_radius then
195	                local distance = storage.dangoreus.flOre[p.name] or 1
196	                local radius = 5
197	                local count = p.surface.count_entities_filtered{
198	                    type = "resource",
199	                    area = {
200	                        {position.x - (radius * distance), position.y - (radius * distance)},
201	                        {position.x + (radius * distance), position.y + (radius * distance)},
202	                    },
203	                }
204	                if count > (distance * radius * 2) ^ 2 * 0.80 then
205	                    storage.dangoreus.flOre[p.name] = math.min(10, distance + 1)
206	                    local target = p.vehicle or p.character
207	                    p.surface.create_entity{
208	                        name = "acid-stream-worm-medium",
209	                        target = target,
210	                        source_position = target.position,
211	                        position = target.position,
212	                        duration = 30,
213	                    }
214	                    target.health = target.health - 15 * distance
215	                    if target.health == 0 then target.die() end
216	                else
217	                    storage.dangoreus.flOre[p.name] = math.max(distance - 2, 1)
218	                end
219	            end
220	        end
221	    end
222	end
223	
224	-- ─── No-op stubs (kept so callers in control.lua keep working) ────────
225	
226	--- Previously built per-surface resource_table; now a no-op because
227	--- clone_mirror handles chunk decoration. Retained as a method so
228	--- existing call sites in control.lua's on_init / on_surface_created
229	--- don't error.
230	function dangoreus.setup_surface(_surface)
231	    -- intentionally empty
232	end
233	
234	return dangoreus
235

4	--

10	-- slot is handed to the next player. force.reset() wipes research (including the
11	-- infinite gl-additional-chunk levels that earned the points) but NOT
12	-- storage.points, so a recycled team would inherit the previous occupant's balance.
13	--
14	-- Gridlocked exposes reset_force(force_index) in its remote interface, which
15	-- resets the balance to the gl-starting-chunks setting and refreshes every member's
16	-- HUD label. We call it on on_team_created and on_team_released so every team
17	-- starts from a clean slate regardless of what the previous occupant did.

20	
21	local M = {}
22	
23	function M.is_active()
24	    return script.active_mods["gridlocked"] ~= nil
25	end

27	local function reset_force_points(force_name)
28	    local force = game.forces[force_name]
29	    if not (force and force.valid) then return end
30	    -- remote_safe.call guards both the interface and the reset_force function
31	    -- existing before calling (CG-2).
32	    remote_safe.call("gridlocked", "reset_force", force.index)
33	end

38	-- clobber each other -- CC-1). Each self-guards on is_active().
39	function M.on_team_created(e)

45	    if not M.is_active() then return end
46	    reset_force_points(e.force_name)

4	--
5	-- Status: PLACEHOLDER. No active code.
6	--
7	-- This file documents the work that would be required to fully support
8	-- the Lignumis planet mod (https://mods.factorio.com/mod/lignumis,
9	-- https://git.cacklingfiend.info/cacklingfiend/lignumis) under MTS's
10	-- per-team planet variants. We deliberately implement nothing today
11	-- because the MTS author isn't actively playing Lignumis. When that
12	-- changes, open this file, decide which gaps actually impact your
13	-- play, and implement only what's needed.
14	--
15	-- ═══ What already works without per-mod compat ════════════════════════
16	--
17	-- Lignumis is a "planets work generically" candidate for everything
18	-- the data-stage enumeration covers. Specifically, MTS already:
19	--
20	--   • Creates per-team variants `mts-lignumis-1..N` at data-final-fixes
21	--     via prototypes/planets.lua. That file iterates data.raw.planet
22	--     dynamically — Lignumis registers its planet through
23	--     PlanetsLib:extend, which ultimately writes to data.raw.planet,
24	--     so the enumeration picks it up.
25	--
26	--   • Builds per-team space-connection variants via
27	--     prototypes/connections.lua. Any base-to-base or base-to-shared
28	--     connection involving lignumis (e.g. nauvis ↔ lignumis) gets N
29	--     team-specific copies.
30	--
31	--   • Routes the planet-discovery-lignumis tech (or any tech with an
32	--     `unlock-space-location` effect targeting "lignumis") to each
33	--     team's variant via scripts/planet_map.lua's
34	--     refresh_discovery_techs() + on_research_finished hook.
35	--
36	--   • Locks/hides the shared base lignumis surface and non-home
37	--     variants from team forces via planet_map.apply_force_locks().
38	--
39	--   • Mirrors decorated chunks from real `lignumis` to each team's
40	--     `mts-lignumis-N` variant via compat/clone_mirror.lua's generic
41	--     `mts-<planet>-<N>` pattern. Worldgen, ambient resources, and
42	--     any chunk-gen mod targeting lignumis flow through automatically.
43	--
44	-- ═══ What's broken: three hardcoded surface-name filters ══════════════
45	--
46	-- Lignumis's runtime control code has three places that filter by
47	-- `surface.name == "lignumis"`. Since MTS team players spend their
48	-- time on `mts-lignumis-N` (not the shared `lignumis`), each of these
49	-- silently no-ops on team surfaces, breaking gameplay:
50	--
51	-- 1. ~/src/lignumis/lignumis/scripts/wooden-rocket-silo.lua:136
52	--    The on_script_trigger_effect handler that registers the
53	--    provisional rocket silo only fires when `event.surface_index`
54	--    equals the literal lignumis surface. On a team variant, the
55	--    silo never registers, so launches from `mts-lignumis-N` don't
56	--    work.
57	--
58	-- 2. ~/src/lignumis/lignumis/scripts/to-nauvis.lua:46
59	--    The "return to Nauvis" teleport triggers only when the player's
60	--    surface is named exactly "lignumis". A team player on
61	--    `mts-lignumis-1` who tries to leave gets stuck — no teleport
62	--    fires.
63	--
64	-- 3. ~/src/lignumis/lignumis/scripts/init.lua:88
65	--    The auto-research gift for automation science pack is gated on
66	--    `player.physical_surface.name ~= "lignumis"`. Players on
67	--    `mts-lignumis-N` either always or never trigger it (depending
68	--    on the comparison direction); either way, behavior diverges
69	--    from the intended single-planet flow.
70	--
71	-- ═══ How to fix each issue ════════════════════════════════════════════
72	--
73	-- The cleanest fix for all three is upstream: change each filter from
74	--
75	--     surface.name == "lignumis"
76	--
77	-- to
78	--
79	--     surface.planet and surface.planet.name == "lignumis"
80	--
81	-- That predicate accepts both the shared `lignumis` and every team
82	-- variant `mts-lignumis-N` (because each variant carries
83	-- `planet="lignumis"` from prototypes/planets.lua's deepcopy). It's a
84	-- generic correctness fix that benefits any planet-renaming mod, not
85	-- just MTS. Same pattern we documented in docs/COMPAT.md.
86	--
87	-- Lignumis is open-source on git.cacklingfiend.info, so a PR is
88	-- realistic. Three small commits, one per file. Cackling Fiend's
89	-- Discord (https://discord.gg/ufvFUJtVwk) is the contact point.
90	--
91	-- If upstream won't accept the change, we'd need to re-implement
92	-- each runtime rule on MTS's side, scoped to team surfaces. Concrete
93	-- shape (NOT IMPLEMENTED, sketch only):
94	--
95	--   • For (1): subscribe to on_script_trigger_effect in MTS, filter
96	--     to events whose effect_id matches Lignumis's silo trigger,
97	--     accept any team-lignumis surface, and replicate the silo
98	--     registration logic on the team surface. Requires
99	--     reverse-engineering or asking the author what the trigger
100	--     does internally.
101	--
102	--   • For (2): subscribe to whatever event Lignumis listens for to
103	--     trigger the to-nauvis teleport (likely a custom-input or
104	--     entity-built event), filter to team lignumis surfaces, and
105	--     run the teleport ourselves. Likely 30-50 lines and brittle to
106	--     Lignumis updates.
107	--
108	--   • For (3): subscribe to on_player_changed_surface, detect
109	--     transitions away from `mts-lignumis-N`, run the auto-research
110	--     grant logic. ~10 lines.
111	--
112	-- All three workarounds are the kind of "re-implement upstream's
113	-- logic" code we explicitly avoid (per docs/COMPAT.md "What MTS
114	-- will not do"). They're a last resort.
115	--
116	-- ═══ What's broken (data-stage) ═══════════════════════════════════════
117	--
118	-- Two more issues that can't be fixed at runtime at all:
119	--
120	-- 4. Ambient sound prototypes are hardcoded to `planet = "lignumis"`
121	--    in ~/src/lignumis/lignumis/prototypes/content/lignumis/planet.lua
122	--    around lines 143-182. Each ambient track only plays on the
123	--    shared lignumis surface, never on team variants. Players on
124	--    `mts-lignumis-N` would get silence instead of the intended
125	--    forest ambiance.
126	--
127	--    Fix would be data-stage: clone each ambient-sound prototype N
128	--    times with `planet = "mts-lignumis-<slot>"`. We'd need MTS's
129	--    prototypes/planets.lua to also iterate ambient sounds (and any
130	--    other prototype types that reference a planet name) for every
131	--    base planet. Significant scope creep.
132	--
133	-- 5. Recipe restrictions are applied via
134	--    PlanetsLib.restrict_to_planet(entity, "lignumis") in
135	--    ~/src/lignumis/lignumis/scripts/wooden-rocket-silo.lua
136	--    around lines 160-162. The restriction only matches the literal
137	--    surface name. Recipes that should only craft on lignumis would
138	--    refuse to craft on team variants.
139	--
140	--    Fix is upstream-only — PlanetsLib.restrict_to_planet's
141	--    implementation would need to accept a list of surface names or
142	--    a planet predicate. Not something MTS can patch from outside.
143	--
144	-- ═══ When to revisit this file ════════════════════════════════════════
145	--
146	-- Open this file when:

1	-- Multi-Team Support - compat/mts_dimension_warp.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Support for the MTS Dimension Warp (MDW) mod. Each team spawns DIRECTLY on
6	-- its own neo-nauvis platform world as warp #0 -- never on nauvis. neo-nauvis
7	-- is MDW's purpose-built hidden starting planet (prototypes/planet/neo-nauvis.lua).
8	--
9	-- Why this is the highest-precedence compat and why it fixes the platform bug
10	-- ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
11	-- nauvis variants are clone-mirrored (compat/clone_mirror.lua), which would
12	-- overwrite the platform tiles MDW lays. neo-nauvis is NOT a clone target, so
13	-- the tiles survive. We therefore create the home as an EPHEMERAL, non-variant
14	-- surface via team_surfaces.create_team_surface. The engine raises
15	-- on_surface_created -> remote_api.raise_team_surface_created -> on_team_surface_created,
16	-- which MDW already listens to and uses to lay the warp platform. So we do NOT
17	-- lay any tiles here; creating the surface is enough to trigger MDW's adoption.
18	--
19	-- Determinism / fairness: every team's warp #0 uses the SAME map_gen_settings
20	-- and the SAME seed (nauvis's seed), so all teams start on an identical world.
21	--
22	-- Surface naming: "mdw-<force>-w0" (e.g. "mdw-team-1-w0"). This is NON-VARIANT:
23	-- it does not match mts-<planet>-N or team-N-<planet>, so normalize_variant_seed
24	-- leaves the caller's seed intact.
25	--
26	-- storage.player_surfaces[player_index] = {name = surface_name, planet = "neo-nauvis"}
27	
28	local compat_utils  = require("compat.compat_utils")
29	local team_surfaces = require("scripts.team_surfaces")
30	local vanilla       = require("compat.vanilla")
31	local helpers       = require("scripts.helpers")
32	-- Control stage does NOT have table.deepcopy by default (it's a data-stage /
33	-- util lualib helper). Require util explicitly for util.table.deepcopy.
34	local util          = require("util")
35	
36	local mts_dimension_warp = {}
37	
38	local NEO_NAUVIS = "neo-nauvis"
39	
40	--- Returns true when MTS Dimension Warp compat should be used.
41	--- Active whenever the mts-dimension-warp mod is loaded.
42	function mts_dimension_warp.is_active()
43	    return script.active_mods["mts-dimension-warp"] ~= nil
44	end
45	
46	mts_dimension_warp.planet_display_name    = compat_utils.planet_display_name
47	-- Reuse the shared teleport path: MDW's pending teleports live in the same
48	-- storage.pending_vanilla_tp queue, so process_pending_teleports == compat_utils'.
49	mts_dimension_warp.process_pending_teleports = compat_utils.process_pending_teleports
50	
51	--- Spawn `player` directly onto their team's neo-nauvis warp #0 platform world.
52	---
53	--- Creates the home via team_surfaces.create_team_surface, which fires
54	--- on_surface_created and lets MDW adopt it + lay the platform tiles. Then we
55	--- stamp player_surfaces / pending_vanilla_tp exactly like compat_utils so the
56	--- deferred teleport (next tick) drops the player onto the new surface.
57	---
58	--- Falls back to vanilla.setup_player_surface if neo-nauvis is missing or the
59	--- create fails, so spawning never hard-fails.
60	function mts_dimension_warp.setup_player_surface(player)
61	    local planet = game.planets and game.planets[NEO_NAUVIS]
62	    if not (planet and planet.valid) then
63	        helpers.diag("mts_dimension_warp.setup_player_surface: neo-nauvis planet "
64	            .. "missing -> vanilla fallback", player)
65	        vanilla.setup_player_surface(player)
66	        return
67	    end
68	
69	    -- Deterministic per-team-identical settings: neo-nauvis's own map_gen plus
70	    -- nauvis's seed, so every team's warp #0 generates the same world (fair).
71	    local mgs = util.table.deepcopy(planet.prototype.map_gen_settings)
72	    local nauvis = game.surfaces["nauvis"]
73	    mgs.seed = nauvis and nauvis.map_gen_settings.seed or 0
74	
75	    local surf_name = team_surfaces.create_team_surface(player.force.name, {
76	        planet           = NEO_NAUVIS,
77	        name             = "mdw-" .. player.force.name .. "-w0",
78	        map_gen_settings = mgs,
79	    })
80	
81	    local surface = surf_name and game.surfaces[surf_name]
82	    if not (surface and surface.valid) then
83	        helpers.diag("mts_dimension_warp.setup_player_surface: create_team_surface "
84	            .. "failed -> vanilla fallback", player)
85	        vanilla.setup_player_surface(player)
86	        return
87	    end
88	
89	    -- Mirror compat_utils.setup_player_surface bookkeeping so the rest of MTS
90	    -- (teleport queue, home lookups) treats this surface as the player's home.
91	    storage.player_surfaces = storage.player_surfaces or {}
92	    storage.player_surfaces[player.index] = {name = surf_name, planet = NEO_NAUVIS}
93	
94	    storage.pending_vanilla_tp = storage.pending_vanilla_tp or {}
95	    storage.pending_vanilla_tp[player.index] = surface
96	end
97	
98	return mts_dimension_warp
99

4	--
5	-- Optional integration with the "Platformer" mod.
6	-- When Platformer is active every player spawns on their own dedicated
7	-- space platform instead of sharing the single "Base One" platform that
8	-- Platformer creates for the default "player" force.
9	--
10	-- Call on_init() from on_init and on_player_created(player) from
11	-- on_player_created, both guarded by is_active().
12	
13	local helpers      = require("scripts.helpers")
14	local spawn_labels = require("scripts.spawn_labels")
15	
16	local platformer = {}
17	
18	--- Character starting items for Platformer mode.
19	--- Edit this list to match Platformer's intended character loadout.
20	--- Hub items are handled separately (see STARTING_ITEMS below).
21	platformer.CHARACTER_STARTING_ITEMS = {
22	    {name = "iron-plate", count = 8},
23	}
24	
25	--- Starting items placed into each player's hub.
26	--- Mirrors Platformer's own set_starting_items() so every personal platform
27	--- begins with the same loadout.
28	local STARTING_ITEMS = {
29	    { name = "crusher",                   count = 1   },
30	    { name = "asteroid-collector",        count = 1   },
31	    { name = "assembling-machine-1",      count = 2   },
32	    { name = "inserter",                  count = 10  },
33	    { name = "solar-panel",               count = 10  },
34	    { name = "space-platform-foundation", count = 100 },
35	    { name = "electric-furnace",          count = 4   },
36	}
37	
38	--- Returns true when the Platformer mod is loaded in the current game.
39	function platformer.is_active()
40	    return script.active_mods["platformer"] ~= nil
41	end
42	
43	--- Create a personal space platform for `player` on their own force,
44	--- populate it with starting items, add a visible name label, and
45	--- teleport the player onto it.
46	---
47	--- Expected call site: on_player_created(), internal use.
48	function platformer.setup_player_platform(player)
49	    local platform_name = player.name .. "'s hub"
50	    local force = player.force
51	
52	    -- Ensure the force has space-platform capability (copied from the
53	    -- default force in create_player_force, but unlock explicitly just
54	    -- in case the copy ran before Platformer finished its own init).
55	    pcall(function() force.unlock_space_platforms() end)
56	
57	    local platform = force.create_space_platform({
58	        name         = platform_name,
59	        planet       = "nauvis",
60	        starter_pack = "space-platform-starter-pack",
61	    })
62	
63	    if not platform then
64	        player.print("[multi-team-support] Could not create personal space platform.")
65	        return
66	    end
67	
68	    platform.apply_starter_pack()
69	
70	    -- Populate hub inventory
71	    local hub = platform.hub
72	    if hub then
73	        for _, item in pairs(STARTING_ITEMS) do
74	            hub.insert(item)
75	        end
76	
77	        -- Draw the persistent team-and-location label anchored to the hub.
78	        -- on_surface_created fires before the hub is placed, so an earlier
79	        -- label may already exist at the default origin position; spawn_labels
80	        -- destroys the old one and re-anchors here.
81	        spawn_labels.draw(force.name, platform.surface, {
82	            target        = hub,
83	            target_offset = { x = 0, y = -2 },
84	        })
85	    end
86	
87	    -- Queue the teleport for the next tick.  Teleporting a characterless
88	    -- player to a freshly created platform surface fails silently when
89	    -- attempted inside on_player_created (the surface isn't ready yet).
90	    if platform.surface then
91	        storage.pending_platform_tp = storage.pending_platform_tp or {}
92	        storage.pending_platform_tp[player.index] = platform.surface
93	    end
94	end
95	
96	--- Process any queued platform teleports.  Must be called from an on_tick
97	--- handler so it runs after on_player_created has fully completed.
98	function platformer.process_pending_teleports()
99	    if not storage.pending_platform_tp then return end
100	    if not next(storage.pending_platform_tp) then return end
101	    for player_index, surface in pairs(storage.pending_platform_tp) do
102	        local player = game.get_player(player_index)
103	        if player and player.valid and surface and surface.valid then
104	            helpers.diag("platformer.process_pending_teleports: TELEPORT → "
105	                .. surface.name, player)
106	            if player.teleport(helpers.ORIGIN, surface) then
107	                storage.pending_platform_tp[player_index] = nil
108	            end
109	        else
110	            storage.pending_platform_tp[player_index] = nil
111	        end
112	    end
113	end
114	
115	--- Handle on_player_created for Platformer compatibility.
116	--- Platformer's own handler runs first (due to optional-dep ordering) and
117	--- teleports the player to its shared "Base One" platform; this overrides
118	--- that by creating each player's personal platform and teleporting them
119	--- there.  Base One is intentionally left alive on the "player" force so
120	--- Platformer's internal storage.platform reference stays valid for all
121	--- future player-join events.  It is hidden from the GUI instead.
122	--- Expected call site: on_player_created (guarded by is_active()).
123	function platformer.on_player_created(player)
124	    platformer.setup_player_platform(player)
125	end
126	
127	return platformer
128

1	-- Multi-Team Support - compat/reassign_player_force.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Generic fix for naturally-generated structures stuck on force="player"
6	-- on team surfaces. Observed cases:
7	--   • Nauvis freeplay crash-site-spaceship-* wreck pieces.
8	--   • Fulgora ruins and the Fulgoran lightning attractor (Space Age).
9	--   • Krastorio 2's kr-spaceship-* additions, plus crash-site-chest-1/2.
10	--   • Any modded equivalent we don't know about yet.
11	--
12	-- The common failure: force="player" entities are not mineable by team
13	-- forces even with set_cease_fire + set_friend. clone_mirror copies these
14	-- entities verbatim from the source planet (where they belong to the real
15	-- "player" force, which has no players in MTS) onto each team surface,
16	-- where they then sit there un-interactable.
17	--
18	-- Fix: after clone_mirror has placed the chunk, sweep every force="player"
19	-- entity in the chunk and reassign it to the team that owns the surface.
20	-- Nothing else is touched — minable and destructible are left at whatever
21	-- the prototype (or another script) set them to, so we don't accidentally
22	-- override an intentional minable=false on a scripted-scenario entity.
23	-- The previous "unmineable" symptom was a pure consequence of the force
24	-- mismatch; once force matches, mining works because the prototype's
25	-- default already says it should.
26	--
27	-- Cross-force diplomacy doesn't enter the picture in MTS because each
28	-- team has its own surface variant (mts-<planet>-<N> / team-<N>-<planet>)
29	-- and only that team's players are ever standing on it — so making the
30	-- team the owner is both safe and preserves entity behavior the team
31	-- would otherwise lose (naturally-spawned power poles wiring into the
32	-- team's electric grid, chests joining the team's logistic network,
33	-- bot-repair on attractors, etc.).
34	--
35	-- Filtering by force is cheap when nothing matches — find_entities_filtered
36	-- returns an empty array without iterating the chunk's full entity set.
37	
38	local surface_utils = require("scripts.surface_utils")
39	
40	local M = {}
41	
42	function M.on_chunk_generated(event)
43	    local surface = event.surface
44	    if not (surface and surface.valid) then return end
45	
46	    local owner = surface_utils.get_owner(surface)
47	    if not owner then return end
48	
49	    for _, entity in pairs(surface.find_entities_filtered{
50	        area  = event.area,
51	        force = "player",
52	    }) do
53	        if entity.valid then
54	            entity.force = owner
55	        end
56	    end
57	end
58	
59	return M
60

4	--
5	-- Dependency-free helper for calling another mod's remote interface defensively.
6	-- Knowing a mod is ACTIVE (script.active_mods) is NOT enough: the interface name
7	-- or a specific function can be renamed/removed between versions, and a bare
8	-- remote.call then hard-errors (often on every player spawn). Route such calls
9	-- through remote_safe.call so a missing interface/function degrades to nil.
10	
11	local remote_safe = {}
12	
13	--- remote.call(interface, fn, ...) only if the interface AND the function exist.
14	--- Returns the call result, or nil if the interface or function is absent.
15	function remote_safe.call(interface, fn, ...)
16	    local iface = remote.interfaces[interface]
17	    if not (iface and iface[fn]) then return nil end
18	    return remote.call(interface, fn, ...)
19	end
20	
21	return remote_safe

31	-- (per-player; SiF applies them itself), and the obsidiax sub-mode

33	-- surface.name == "nauvis" and would also need generalizing.
34	
35	
36	local M = {}
37	
38	function M.is_active()
39	    return script.active_mods["space-is-fake"] ~= nil
40	end
41	
42	-- Box-platform tile per alternate map setting. The default "sif" map keeps
43	-- "stone-path" (no box repaint), matching SiF: only these settings repaint.
44	local BOX_TILE = {
45	    vulcanus = "volcanic-cracks-warm",
46	    fulgora  = "fulgoran-rock",
47	    gleba    = "natural-yumako-soil",
48	    aquilo   = "snow-flat",
49	    pelagos  = "pelagos-sand-1",
50	    lignumis = "natural-gold-soil",
51	}
52	
53	local TREE_POSITIONS = {
54	    { -28, 28 }, { -16, 28 }, { -8, 28 }, { 2, 28 }, { 12, 28 }, { 22, 28 },
55	    { -28, 36 }, { -18, 36 }, { -8, 36 }, { 4, 36 }, { 12, 36 }, { 22, 36 },
56	    { 14, 28 }, { 24, 28 }, { -26, 30 }, { -26, 32 }, { -16, 32 }, { 24, 32 },
57	    { 4,  34 }, { -6, 36 }, { 14, 36 }, { 24, 36 }, { -28, 30 }, { -18, 30 },
58	    { -8, 30 }, { 2, 30 }, { 14, 30 }, { 22, 30 }, { -28, 32 }, { -18, 32 },
59	    { -8, 32 }, { 2, 32 }, { 14, 32 }, { 22, 32 }, { -28, 34 }, { -18, 34 },
60	    { -8, 34 }, { 14, 34 }, { -22, 28 }, { -14, 28 }, { -2, 28 }, { 8, 28 },
61	    { 18, 28 }, { 28, 28 }, { -22, 36 }, { -12, 36 }, { 6, 36 }, { -2, 36 },
62	    { 18, 36 }, { 28, 36 }, { 16, 28 }, { 26, 28 }, { -24, 32 }, { -14, 32 },
63	    { 26, 32 }, { -24, 34 }, { 6, 34 }, { -4, 36 }, { 16, 36 }, { 26, 36 },

65	    { -12, 32 }, { -2, 32 }, { 8, 32 }, { 16, 32 }, { 28, 32 }, { -22, 34 },
66	    { -12, 34 }, { -2, 34 }, { 16, 34 }, { 28, 34 }

69	local function is_lava(tile_name)
70	    return tile_name == "lava" or tile_name == "lava-hot"
71	end
72	
73	-- Paint volcanic ash over lava tiles just inside a water edge, within
74	-- `radius` of `center`. Faithful to SiF's lava-edge pass.
75	local function paint_lava_ash(surface, center)
76	    local radius = 200
77	    local area = {
78	        { center.x - radius, center.y - radius },
79	        { center.x + radius, center.y + radius },
80	    }
81	    local dirs = { { 1, 0 }, { -1, 0 }, { 0, 1 }, { 0, -1 } }
82	    local set_tiles = {}
83	    for _, tile in pairs(surface.find_tiles_filtered{ area = area, name = "water" }) do
84	        local tx, ty = tile.position.x, tile.position.y
85	        for _, d in pairs(dirs) do
86	            local neighbor = surface.get_tile(tx + d[1], ty + d[2])
87	            if neighbor and is_lava(neighbor.name) then
88	                for i = 1, 2 do
89	                    local lx, ly = tx + d[1] * i, ty + d[2] * i
90	                    local lava = surface.get_tile(lx, ly)
91	                    if lava and is_lava(lava.name) then
92	                        set_tiles[#set_tiles + 1] =
93	                            { name = "volcanic-ash-dark", position = { lx, ly } }
94	                    end
95	                end
96	            end
97	        end
98	    end
99	    if #set_tiles > 0 then surface.set_tiles(set_tiles, true) end
100	end
101	
102	-- Repaint the starting platform box for alternate map settings (no-op for the
103	-- default "sif" map), clearing decoratives and rocks from it as SiF does.
104	local function paint_box(surface, map_setting)
105	    local box_tile = BOX_TILE[map_setting]
106	    if not box_tile then return end
107	    local tiles = {}
108	    for x = -33, 32 do
109	        for y = 23, 40 do
110	            tiles[#tiles + 1] = { name = box_tile, position = { x, y } }
111	        end
112	    end
113	    surface.set_tiles(tiles, true)
114	    local box_area = { { -33, 23 }, { 32, 40 } }
115	    surface.destroy_decoratives{ area = box_area }
116	    for _, entity in pairs(surface.find_entities_filtered{ area = box_area, type = "simple-entity" }) do
117	        if entity.valid then entity.destroy() end
118	    end
119	end
120	
121	-- Place SiF's full starting layout on `surface`, centered on the spawn at
122	-- `center`. SiF splits tiles (player.surface) and entities (game.surfaces.
123	-- nauvis) across two surfaces; on a single team variant the two coincide.
124	local function place_starting_area(surface, center)
125	    paint_lava_ash(surface, center)
126	    paint_box(surface, settings.startup["sif-map"].value)
127	
128	    for _, pos in ipairs(TREE_POSITIONS) do
129	        surface.create_entity{ name = "tree-plant", position = pos, force = "neutral" }
130	    end
131	
132	    local chest = surface.create_entity{ name = "dead-engineer", position = { 4, 10 }, force = "neutral" }
133	    if chest and chest.valid then
134	        local inv = chest.get_inventory(defines.inventory.chest)
135	        if inv then
136	            inv.insert{ name = "lucky-coin", count = 6 }
137	            inv.insert{ name = "scrap", count = 50 }
138	            inv.insert{ name = "cliff-explosives", count = 20 }
139	        end
140	    end
141	
142	    if settings.startup["space-is-fake-zstorm"].value then
143	        surface.create_entity{ name = "fulgoran-ruin-attractor", position = { 0, 8 }, force = "neutral" }
144	    end
145	end
146	
147	-- Called from compat_utils.process_pending_teleports, once the player is on
148	-- their team surface. Sets up the SiF starting area on the team's Nauvis
149	-- variant exactly once (guard keyed by surface name).
150	function M.after_spawn(player)
151	    if not M.is_active() then return end
152	    if not (player and player.valid) then return end
153	    local surface = player.surface
154	    if not (surface and surface.valid) then return end
155	
156	    -- Only the team's Nauvis variant. SiF requires Space Age, so the home
157	    -- surface is "mts-nauvis-<N>"; "team-<N>-nauvis" matched as defence-in-depth.
158	    local base = surface.name:match("^mts%-(.+)%-%d+$")
159	              or surface.name:match("^team%-%d+%-(.+)$")
160	    if base ~= "nauvis" then return end
161	
162	    storage.sif_setup_done = storage.sif_setup_done or {}
163	    if storage.sif_setup_done[surface.name] then return end
164	    storage.sif_setup_done[surface.name] = true
165	
166	    place_starting_area(surface, player.position)
167	end
168	
169	-- Fanned out from the single MTS-owned on_team_released dispatcher in
170	-- events/ticks.lua (see CC-1). Clears the setup guard for the released slot's
171	-- surface names by the deterministic slot number, NOT by game.surfaces
172	-- existence: game.delete_surface is deferred, so this same-tick handler still
173	-- sees the surface, and the old existence check never cleared it -- leaving the
174	-- recycled slot's fresh surface without SiF starting-area setup (ST-1).
175	function M.on_team_released(e)
176	    if not M.is_active() then return end
177	    if not storage.sif_setup_done then return end
178	    local slot = e.force_name:match("^team%-(%d+)$")
179	    if not slot then return end
180	    storage.sif_setup_done["mts-nauvis-" .. slot]        = nil  -- SA home variant
181	    storage.sif_setup_done["team-" .. slot .. "-nauvis"] = nil  -- non-SA fallback
182	end
183	
184	return M

1	-- Multi-Team Support - compat/ultracube.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Compatibility with the Ultracube overhaul mod by grandseiken.
6	-- https://mods.factorio.com/mod/Ultracube
7	--
8	-- Architecture
9	-- ────────────
10	-- Ultracube normally initialises players (cube creation, starting armor) in
11	-- its on_player_created handler. In MTS, players are created before force
12	-- assignment completes: with the landing pen they arrive on the spectator
13	-- force, and even without it the force transition happens in the same tick
14	-- just after the event fires. Acting at on_player_created would therefore
15	-- place the starting cube on the wrong force.
16	--
17	-- Ultracube exposes two remote calls for this situation:
18	--   • disable_auto_player_setup() — suppresses its own on_player_created
19	--     handler so we can drive the timing ourselves.
20	--   • setup_player(player_index)  — runs the per-player setup (equip armor)
21	--     and the per-force first-time setup (place starting cube) for whatever
22	--     force the player is currently on.
23	--
24	-- We call disable_auto_player_setup() once during on_init. setup_player() is
25	-- called via after_spawn() at each spawn site, after the player has been
26	-- teleported onto their team surface. Calling it at on_player_joined_team
27	-- would be too early — the teleport is deferred and the player's surface
28	-- is still the landing pen at that point, which would place the cube there.
29	--
30	-- Force recycling
31	-- ───────────────
32	-- MTS recycles force slots when a team disbands: force.reset() is called
33	-- and the slot returns to the pool for a future team. Ultracube tracks
34	-- per-force state (cube_given, victory_state) keyed by force name. Without
35	-- cleanup, a recycled slot retains the old team's flags and the new team
36	-- never gets a starting cube or a chance to win.
37	--
38	-- We call reset_force(force_name) when on_team_released fires, which clears
39	-- those flags so the next team to claim the slot starts fresh.
40	
41	local remote_safe = require("compat.remote_safe")
42	
43	local ultracube = {}
44	
45	function ultracube.is_active()
46	    return script.active_mods["Ultracube"] ~= nil
47	end
48	
49	-- Called from on_init and on_configuration_changed.
50	function ultracube.on_init()
51	    if not ultracube.is_active() then return end
52	    if not (remote.interfaces["Ultracube"] and
53	            remote.interfaces["Ultracube"]["disable_auto_player_setup"]) then
54	        return
55	    end
56	    remote.call("Ultracube", "disable_auto_player_setup")
57	end
58	
59	-- Called at every spawn site immediately after the player has been
60	-- teleported onto their team surface. At this point player.surface is
61	-- the correct team surface, so Ultracube will place the starting cube
62	-- there rather than on the landing pen or whatever intermediate surface
63	-- the player was on when force assignment happened.
64	function ultracube.after_spawn(player)
65	    if not ultracube.is_active() then return end
66	    if not (remote.interfaces["Ultracube"] and
67	            remote.interfaces["Ultracube"]["setup_player"]) then
68	        return
69	    end
70	    remote.call("Ultracube", "setup_player", player.index)
71	end
72	
73	-- Fanned out from the single MTS-owned on_team_released dispatcher in
74	-- events/ticks.lua (see CC-1 -- shims can't each register the same event id).
75	function ultracube.on_team_released(e)
76	    if not ultracube.is_active() then return end
77	    -- The force slot is being recycled. Clear Ultracube's per-force flags so the
78	    -- next team to claim this slot gets a fresh starting cube and an unblocked
79	    -- victory condition. remote_safe.call guards interface + function existence.
80	    remote_safe.call("Ultracube", "reset_force", e.force_name)
81	end
82	
83	return ultracube
84

4	--
5	-- Support for vanilla-style games (no Platformer mod) where each player
6	-- spawns on their own fresh copy of the Nauvis surface generated from the
7	-- same seed as the shared Nauvis, giving everyone an identical starting world.
8	--
9	-- Surface naming: "<force_name>-<planet>" e.g. "force-bob-nauvis"
10	-- Using force name (not player name/index) so the surface is identifiable
11	-- by its owning force, which supports multi-player teams in the future.
12	--
13	-- storage.player_surfaces[player_index] = {name = surface_name, planet = "nauvis"}
14	
15	local compat_utils = require("compat.compat_utils")
16	
17	local vanilla = {}
18	
19	--- Returns true when vanilla surface compat should be used.
20	--- Active whenever the Platformer mod is NOT loaded.
21	function vanilla.is_active()
22	    return script.active_mods["platformer"] == nil
23	end
24	
25	vanilla.planet_display_name    = compat_utils.planet_display_name
26	vanilla.process_pending_teleports = compat_utils.process_pending_teleports
27	
28	--- Create a personal Nauvis surface for `player` using the same map-gen
29	--- settings as the shared "nauvis" surface (same seed, fresh world state).
30	--- The surface will generate terrain identically to the original Nauvis but
31	--- is completely independent — only this player's force can see it.
32	---
33	--- Teleport is deferred to the next tick via storage.pending_vanilla_tp so
34	--- it is safe to call from on_player_created before the character is ready.
35	function vanilla.setup_player_surface(player)
36	    compat_utils.setup_player_surface(player, function(surf_name, planet)
37	        local nauvis = game.surfaces[planet]
38	        local mgs    = nauvis and nauvis.map_gen_settings or {}
39	        local surface = game.create_surface(surf_name, mgs)
40	
41	        -- Pre-generate spawn-area chunks BEFORE the player teleports.
42	        -- clone_mirror.on_chunk_generated runs synchronously here for
43	        -- each generated chunk and calls LuaSurface.clone_area, which
44	        -- overwrites destination contents — including any character
45	        -- entity at the player's position. Doing the work up front
46	        -- means clone_area runs on an empty surface, so the player's
47	        -- character (placed during the deferred teleport on the next
48	        -- tick) lands on already-cloned terrain instead of being
49	        -- evicted by an in-flight clone.
50	        surface.request_to_generate_chunks({0, 0}, 3)
51	        surface.force_generate_chunk_requests()
52	
53	        return surface
54	    end)
55	end
56	
57	return vanilla
58

4	--
5	-- Data-stage compat shim for the "belt-ban" mod (No Belts - Challenge Mode).
6	--
7	-- belt-ban disables the logistics / logistics-2 / logistics-3 technologies
8	-- (enabled = false) to strip out every transport belt. A disabled prerequisite
9	-- can never be satisfied, so that permanently orphans three important NON-belt
10	-- technologies that list logistics-2 as a prerequisite:
11	--
12	--   * automobilism   (car)
13	--   * bulk-inserter  (bulk inserter + capacity bonus)
14	--   * railway        (rails, locomotive, wagons)
15	--
16	-- We remove "logistics-2" from those three techs' prerequisites so they
17	-- reconnect to the tree through their OTHER prerequisites (engine /
18	-- fast-inserter / advanced-circuit), all of which stay researchable. Belts
19	-- themselves remain banned: we never touch logistics-2's own enabled flag.
20	--
21	-- Order relative to belt-ban does not matter -- belt-ban never edits these
22	-- three techs' prerequisites, so stripping logistics-2 here is independent of
23	-- whichever mod's data-final-fixes runs first.
24	
25	-- tech name -> prerequisite to strip
26	local STRIP = {
27	    ["automobilism"]  = "logistics-2",
28	    ["bulk-inserter"] = "logistics-2",
29	    ["railway"]       = "logistics-2",
30	}
31	
32	--- Remove `prereq` from `tech`'s prerequisites, if both exist.
33	local function strip_prerequisite(tech_name, prereq)
34	    local tech = data.raw.technology[tech_name]
35	    if not tech or not tech.prerequisites then return end
36	    for i = #tech.prerequisites, 1, -1 do
37	        if tech.prerequisites[i] == prereq then
38	            table.remove(tech.prerequisites, i)
39	        end
40	    end
41	end
42	
43	for tech_name, prereq in pairs(STRIP) do
44	    strip_prerequisite(tech_name, prereq)
45	end

1	-- Multi-Team Support - prototypes/connections.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Data-stage (final-fixes): creates per-team space-connection prototypes
6	-- by mirroring the vanilla connection topology for each team slot.
7	--
8	-- For every existing space-connection prototype we classify the endpoints:
9	--
10	--   base  ↔ base  (e.g. "nauvis-vulcanus", "lignumis-vulcanus")
11	--       Generate N variants, each between the team's planet variants:
12	--       team 1: mts-nauvis-1 ↔ mts-vulcanus-1, etc.
13	--
14	--   base  ↔ shared (e.g. "aquilo-solar-system-edge")
15	--       The shared endpoint (solar-system-edge, shattered-planet) is NOT
16	--       duplicated per team — it's a single shared location every team
17	--       travels to. We generate N variants that rewrite only the planet
18	--       side: team 1: mts-aquilo-1 ↔ solar-system-edge, etc. This mirrors
19	--       the Team Starts mod's approach and is what lets each team reach
20	--       the endgame edge and shattered-planet locations.
21	--
22	--   shared ↔ shared (e.g. "solar-system-edge-shattered-planet")
23	--       No per-team variants needed — the vanilla prototype is already
24	--       team-agnostic. Every team uses the same connection.
25	--
26	--   anything else (a connection where neither endpoint is a known
27	--   planet or shared location — possible if a mod registers a
28	--   connection to a custom space-location prototype we don't know
29	--   about): skipped. The base connection still exists for everyone.
30	--
31	-- Modded planet connections work automatically: we iterate every
32	-- connection in `data.raw["space-connection"]` and classify by endpoint.
33	-- A planet mod that adds Lignumis with a connection to Nauvis will
34	-- have both endpoints recognized (lignumis is in data.raw.planet,
35	-- nauvis is in data.raw.planet) and generate per-team variants.
36	
37	local space_age = require("scripts.space_age")
38	
39	assert(data.raw["space-connection"], "connections.lua: no space-connection prototypes loaded")
40	
41	local max_teams = settings.startup["mts_max_teams"].value
42	
43	-- Build a set of base-planet names for quick membership check. Uses the
44	-- same enumeration as planets.lua so the variant set and the connection
45	-- variant set stay in sync — a planet that gets variants always also
46	-- gets connection variants (and vice versa).
47	local base_set = {}
48	for _, name in ipairs(space_age.list_base_planets_data()) do
49	    base_set[name] = true
50	end
51	
52	-- Space Age endgame locations that are shared across all teams. They
53	-- appear as connection endpoints but are never duplicated per team.
54	local SHARED_LOCATIONS = {
55	    ["solar-system-edge"] = true,
56	    ["shattered-planet"]  = true,
57	}
58	
59	local function is_base(name)   return base_set[name] == true end
60	local function is_shared(name) return SHARED_LOCATIONS[name] == true end
61	
62	--- Look up the icon for an endpoint across planet and space-location
63	--- prototype tables. Planets live in data.raw.planet; shared locations
64	--- (solar-system-edge, shattered-planet) live in data.raw["space-location"].
65	local function endpoint_icon(name)
66	    local p = data.raw.planet and data.raw.planet[name]
67	    if p and p.icon then return p.icon, p.icon_size end
68	    local s = data.raw["space-location"] and data.raw["space-location"][name]
69	    if s and s.icon then return s.icon, s.icon_size end
70	    return nil
71	end
72	
73	--- Build a dynamic icon stack for a connection using the two endpoint icons.
74	--- Falls back to the base connection's icons if either endpoint lookup fails.
75	local function make_icons(from_name, to_name, base_icons)
76	    local from_icon, from_sz = endpoint_icon(from_name)
77	    local to_icon,   to_sz   = endpoint_icon(to_name)
78	    if not (from_icon and to_icon) then
79	        return base_icons
80	    end
81	    return {
82	        {icon = from_icon, icon_size = from_sz or 64,
83	         scale = 1 / 3, shift = {-6, -6}},
84	        {icon = to_icon,   icon_size = to_sz or 64,
85	         scale = 1 / 3, shift = { 6,  6}},
86	    }
87	end
88	
89	-- Snapshot existing connections BEFORE we extend data.raw (avoid iterating
90	-- over our own newly-added prototypes). Keep only connections we plan to
91	-- variantise: base↔base and base↔shared. Shared↔shared stays as vanilla.
92	local base_connections = {}
93	for name, conn in pairs(data.raw["space-connection"]) do
94	    if conn.from and conn.to then
95	        local from_base   = is_base(conn.from)
96	        local to_base     = is_base(conn.to)
97	        local from_shared = is_shared(conn.from)
98	        local to_shared   = is_shared(conn.to)
99	        local keep = (from_base and to_base)

4	--
5	-- A hidden, powerless passive radar that other MTS-aware mods place (via the
6	-- mts-v1 `ensure_passive_radar` interface) to keep a team surface live-viewable
7	-- when nobody is standing on it.
8	--
9	-- WHY this exists: a remote/map view only renders chunks that are CHARTED and
10	-- fog-free for the viewing force. An empty team surface has no standing vision
11	-- source, so a spectator (a chart-sharing friend of the team) sees a black
12	-- screen. A character provides live vision; so does a radar. We want a radar's
13	-- reveal WITHOUT a real radar's power cost or unbounded map charting.
14	--
15	-- The Factorio radar prototype has two reveal mechanisms:
16	--   max_distance_of_nearby_sector_revealed = a ring kept revealed while working.
17	--   max_distance_of_sector_revealed        = a rotating scan that charts sector
18	--       by sector out to this radius.
19	-- The save-bloat hazard is a LARGE sector radius (e.g. vanilla 14) that charts
20	-- the whole explored map over time. We bound BOTH to the same small radius, so
21	-- the radar only ever reveals/charts a fixed local bubble around itself -- enough
22	-- to make the floor viewable, but it never expands to chart the wider map (no
23	-- unbounded save growth). We deliberately keep the sector scan ON (not 0): a
24	-- nearby-only reveal proved unreliable in practice, and a bounded sector scan
25	-- guarantees the floor is actually revealed. Powered from a `void` source so it
26	-- needs no electricity and never shows in the power graph. Reused by MDW
27	-- (dimension floors / docks) and BNM. Consumers place several across a base
28	-- larger than one bubble.
29	
30	local radar = table.deepcopy(data.raw["radar"]["radar"])
31	
32	radar.name = "mts-passive-radar"
33	
34	-- Invisible + inert: no icon, no collision, no selection, no map marker, no
35	-- player interaction. It is placed by script and never seen or touched.
36	radar.icon       = nil
37	radar.icon_size  = nil
38	radar.icons      = {util.empty_icon()}
39	radar.collision_box = {{0, 0}, {0, 0}}
40	radar.selection_box = {{0, 0}, {0, 0}}
41	radar.collision_mask = {layers = {}}
42	radar.flags = {
43	    "placeable-off-grid",
44	    "not-on-map",
45	    "not-blueprintable",
46	    "not-deconstructable",
47	    "not-upgradable",
48	    "not-flammable",
49	    "not-in-kill-statistics",
50	}
51	radar.hidden = true
52	radar.hidden_in_factoriopedia = true
53	radar.working_sound = nil
54	radar.minable = nil
55	radar.placeable_by = nil
56	radar.radius_minimap_visualisation_color = nil
57	radar.integration_patch = nil
58	radar.water_reflection = nil
59	
60	-- Free power, no emissions: a hidden utility radar must not aggravate biters or
61	-- show up in the pollution stats. Cheap per-scan energy + a fast usage rate so the
62	-- bounded scan reveals the local bubble quickly (the void source has effectively
63	-- unlimited buffer, so these only set the work cadence, not a real cost).
64	radar.energy_source = {type = "void", emissions_per_minute = {}}
65	radar.energy_usage = "50kW"
66	radar.energy_per_sector = "10kJ"
67	radar.energy_per_nearby_scan = "10kJ"

70	-- bounded to the same small radius (8 chunks ~= 512 tiles across). The scan is the
71	-- part that actually guarantees the floor is charted/viewable; bounding it to a
72	-- fixed radius means it never crawls outward to chart the wider map, so there is no
73	-- unbounded save growth. Consumers place several radars to cover a base larger than
74	-- one bubble.
75	radar.max_distance_of_nearby_sector_revealed = 8
76	radar.max_distance_of_sector_revealed = 8
77	
78	-- No visible graphics — placed and seen only by the engine's reveal logic.
