80	    layers = {
81	        {
82	            filename = "__core__/graphics/empty.png",
83	            priority = "extra-high",

1	-- Multi-Team Support - prototypes/entities/passivize-radars.lua
2	-- Author: bits-orio
3	-- License: GPL-3.0-or-later
4	--
5	-- Turns every "scanning" radar into a passive one: it keeps the local ring it
6	-- always reveals while working (max_distance_of_nearby_sector_revealed) but no
7	-- longer runs the rotating sector scan (max_distance_of_sector_revealed) that
8	-- permanently charts chunks far out from the radar.
9	--
10	-- WHY: on a multi-team server each team blankets its territory with radars, and
11	-- an active radar permanently charts a ~14-chunk-radius disc; the union across
12	-- ~20 teams is a serious save-size and UPS sink. Passivizing bounds that growth
13	-- while preserving the thing players actually place radars for -- a stable patch
14	-- of local visibility.
15	--
16	-- Gated by the "mts_passive_radars" startup setting (default on). Runs at
17	-- data-final-fixes so it also catches radars added by other mods.
18	--
19	-- Mechanism: clamp the sector-scan radius DOWN to the radar's own nearby-reveal
20	-- radius. This is deliberately not "set to 0":
21	--   * Setting the sector scan to 0 proved unreliable in practice (see the note
22	--     in passive-radar.lua) -- a bounded scan equal to the nearby ring reliably
23	--     charts exactly the local bubble and never crawls outward.
24	--   * Clamping to each radar's OWN nearby radius makes the rule self-preserving:
25	--     our hidden mts-passive-radar (nearby 8 / sector 8) is left untouched, and
26	--     any modded radar keeps its intended local footprint.
27	--   * Radars with no nearby reveal (nearby == 0) are purpose-built scanners
28	--     whose entire job is charting; clamping them to 0 would make them useless
29	--     rather than passive, so we leave them alone.
30	-- Energy: ONLY the base-game radar is dropped to 50 kW (from 300 kW) -- with no
31	-- wide sector scan to run it does far less work. Modded radars keep their own
32	-- energy_usage untouched: a flat 50 kW would flatten deliberate mod tiers (e.g.
33	-- K2's 2 MW advanced radar sustaining an 8-chunk bubble would cost the same as
34	-- a vanilla radar). The scan clamp alone already delivers the save-bloat fix,
35	-- which is this feature's goal -- rebalancing other mods' power economy is not.
36	
37	local PASSIVE_ENERGY_USAGE = "50kW"
38	
39	if not settings.startup["mts_passive_radars"].value then return end
40	
41	for _, radar in pairs(data.raw["radar"] or {}) do
42	    local nearby = radar.max_distance_of_nearby_sector_revealed or 0
43	    local sector = radar.max_distance_of_sector_revealed or 0
44	    if nearby > 0 and sector > nearby then
45	        radar.max_distance_of_sector_revealed = nearby
46	        if radar.name == "radar" then
47	            radar.energy_usage = PASSIVE_ENERGY_USAGE
48	        end
49	
50	        -- Relabel so the tooltip matches the new behavior. Prefix the radar's
51	        -- OWN name (fall back to its entity-name key when it has no explicit
52	        -- localised_name) so vanilla reads "Passive Radar" while a modded radar
53	        -- keeps its identity ("Passive <Name>") instead of all collapsing to one
54	        -- label. Description is replaced with the generic passive one. The
55	        -- locale keys are "mts-passivized-*", deliberately NOT the hidden
56	        -- mts-passive-radar entity's name, so they never alias its own
57	        -- entity-name/entity-description lookups.
58	        local orig_name = radar.localised_name or {"entity-name." .. radar.name}
59	        radar.localised_name = {"entity-name.mts-passivized-radar-prefix", orig_name}
60	        radar.localised_description = {"entity-description.mts-passivized-radar"}
61	
62	        -- Rename the placer item(s) to match. Items without an explicit
63	        -- localised_name usually inherit the entity name via place_result, but
64	        -- a mod that ships an explicit item-name locale entry would otherwise
65	        -- keep its stale label in the inventory/crafting menu while the placed
66	        -- entity says "Passive". Recipes follow their main product, so they
67	        -- pick this up for free. (Radar placers are plain "item" prototypes.)
68	        for _, item in pairs(data.raw["item"] or {}) do
69	            if item.place_result == radar.name then
70	                item.localised_name =
71	                    {"entity-name.mts-passivized-radar-prefix", orig_name}
72	            end
73	        end
74	    end
75	end

2	-- Author: bits-orio

4	--
5	-- Data-stage: creates per-team planet variants by deep-copying every base
6	-- planet prototype currently in `data.raw.planet`, N times, where
7	-- N = mts_max_teams startup setting.
8	--
9	-- Each variant is a full planet prototype with:
10	--   • unique name: "mts-<base>-<slot>" e.g. "mts-nauvis-1"
11	--   • the base planet's own map_seed_offset (kept from the deepcopy), so
12	--     every team's variant generates identical terrain — including
13	--     territory demolishers, which clone_mirror can't replicate
14	--   • orientation offset so they don't overlap visually in the solar
15	--     system view
16	--
17	-- Why iterate `data.raw.planet` instead of a hardcoded list
18	-- ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
19	-- Hardcoding {nauvis, vulcanus, gleba, fulgora, aquilo} excluded modded
20	-- planets (Maraxsis, Lignumis, Muluna, etc.) from variant creation —
21	-- teams would all share the modded planet, defeating the per-team
22	-- isolation MTS provides. Iterating the live prototype table picks up
23	-- every planet the mod stack has registered by data-final-fixes.
24	--
25	-- Load-order requirement: any mod (or planet library) that registers
26	-- planets must do so by data-final-fixes. Mods that depend on
27	-- PlanetsLib already follow this pattern. To guarantee MTS sees them,
28	-- info.json declares `? PlanetsLib` and similar libraries as optional
29	-- dependencies — Factorio resolves optional deps to "load before" so
30	-- their data stages complete before MTS iterates here.
31	--
32	-- The base planets themselves are left intact; they are locked for
33	-- team forces at runtime so teams can only see/reach their own
34	-- variants. See scripts/planet_map.lua's apply_force_locks.
35	
36	local space_age = require("scripts.space_age")
37	
38	assert(data.raw.planet, "planets.lua: data.raw.planet is missing")
39	
40	local max_teams = settings.startup["mts_max_teams"].value
41	
42	-- Small orientation offsets for vanilla base planets so our variants
43	-- cluster away from the visual positions of the base planet in the
44	-- space map. Values are angles on the 0..1 unit circle. Modded
45	-- planets fall through to 0; their variants get spread around the
46	-- ring purely by slot index, which is fine in practice (tested with
47	-- a few modded-planet combos at 20 teams; no visible overlap).
48	local BASE_ORIENT_OFFSET = {
49	    nauvis   = 0.02,
50	    vulcanus = 0.00,
51	    gleba    = 0.00,
52	    fulgora  = 0.08,
53	    aquilo   = 0.04,
54	}
55	
56	for _, base_name in ipairs(space_age.list_base_planets_data()) do
57	    local base = data.raw.planet[base_name]
58	    -- list_base_planets_data() guarantees the entry exists, but we
59	    -- guard anyway in case a mod removes a planet between the
60	    -- enumeration and our access (rare; defensive).
61	    if base then
62	        local base_orient = BASE_ORIENT_OFFSET[base_name] or 0
63	        for slot = 1, max_teams do
64	            local variant = table.deepcopy(base)
65	            variant.name = space_age.variant_name(base_name, slot)
66	
67	            -- Use the base planet's own seed (not a random one). With the same
68	            -- seed and the same map_gen_settings, every team's variant generates
69	            -- byte-identical terrain on its own — including territory demolishers,
70	            -- which clone_mirror cannot replicate (clone_area destroys segmented
71	            -- units). This keeps the outer planets consistent across teams WITHOUT
72	            -- cloning, so their native demolishers survive. Nauvis is still cloned
73	            -- (its base surface always exists), so its variants stay identical via
74	            -- clone_mirror regardless of seed.
75	            variant.map_seed_offset = base.map_seed_offset
76	
77	            -- Keep the variant's order grouped with its base planet
78	            -- in menus (so e.g. "mts-nauvis-1..N" appear next to
79	            -- "nauvis" in any list view that respects order strings).
80	            local original_order = type(base.order) == "string" and base.order or "z"
81	            variant.order = string.format("%s[%s]", original_order, variant.name)
82	
83	            -- Spread variants around the solar-system ring so they
84	            -- don't stack on top of each other in the space map view.
85	            local offset = base_orient + (slot / (max_teams + 1))
86	            variant.orientation = offset % 1
87	            variant.label_orientation = offset % 1
88	
89	            -- Localisation: without an explicit localised_name,
90	            -- Factorio tries to look up
91	            -- `space-location-name.mts-<base>-<slot>` which doesn't
92	            -- exist, producing "Unknown key" warnings everywhere.
93	            -- We concatenate the base planet's localised name with
94	            -- the slot number: e.g. "Vulcanus 1", "Nauvis 2",
95	            -- "Lignumis 3". This works for any planet that has a
96	            -- `space-location-name.<base>` locale entry — vanilla
97	            -- planets and well-behaved modded ones both qualify.
98	            variant.localised_name = {
99	                "", {"space-location-name." .. base_name}, " " .. slot,
100	            }
101	            variant.localised_description = {
102	                "space-location-description." .. base_name,
103	            }
104	
105	            data:extend{variant}
106	        end
107	    end
108	end
